customer_name: Creating Animal Respect Education Foundation dba CARE Fo

citations.narrative:
The enclosure housing one white-throated capuchin and two brown capuchins has 8 bolts that could injure the non-
human primates. The bolts attach the shelter enclosure to the cage enclosure at the capuchins’ door. These bolts are
spaced vertically on either side of the entry door. The bolts extend into the monkey’s space 1/2-2 inches.
The bolts could injure an eye or catch and tear the skin of a capuchin moving toward the door. Primary enclosures must
be constructed and maintained so that they have no sharp points or edges that could injure the nonhuman primates.
Correct by September 3, 2026

The entry gate to the area containing one tiger enclosure and one liger hybrid enclosure APHIS officials measured a 12-
inch gap between the bottom of the gate and the ground. The perimeter fence must be constructed so that it protects the
animals in the facility by restricting animals and unauthorized persons from going through it or under it and having contact
with animals in the facility, and so that it can function as a secondary containment system for the animals in the facility. A
gap of that size can allow animals in or out and does not protect the animals in the facility by restricting animals from
going under it or act as secondary containment for the animals in the facility. All outdoor housing facilities must be
enclosed by a perimeter fence in order to ensure the welfare of the animals under the Animal Welfare Act.
Correct by September 10, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
